topic: Displacement and Velocity Using Distance-Time Graphs
key_concepts: Motion can be described using distance-time and displacement-time graphs.
The slope of a distance-time graph represents speed.
The slope of a displacement-time graph represents velocity.
Slope is calculated as change in distance or displacement divided by change in time.
Uniform motion appears as a straight line on a distance-time graph.
A zero slope on a displacement-time graph means the object is at rest.
A positive slope indicates motion away from the starting point.
A negative slope indicates motion toward the starting point.
Average speed is total distance divided by total time.
Different slopes over time intervals show changes in motion.
